# Cal.com Ingestion Pipeline — Spec

## Overview

Build a Cal.com ingestion pipeline at the top level of `gtm-sdk/` that receives booking webhook payloads via a Modal `fastapi_endpoint`, validates them against Pydantic models derived from the Cal.com OpenAPI schema, and persists raw plus ETL'd records to GCS. Architecture mirrors `tmp/gtm/src/services/fathom/`. **Only the two runners Cal.com Phase 1 invokes (`export_to_gcp_etl`, `export_to_gcp_raw`) are vendored from Fathom**; the `export_to_modal_storage` and `export_to_lancedb` runners stay in `tmp/gtm/` and are ported in Phase 2 alongside their dependencies (`gemini/`, `lance/`). The `Webhook` model still implements the full Fathom contract — `lance_*` / `storage_*` methods raise `NotImplementedError` so the contract is intact when those runners arrive.

## Trigger & Scope

- **Trigger:** Cal.com booking webhook events delivered as HTTP POST to a Modal `fastapi_endpoint`, fronted by a webhook middle layer (Hookdeck-style) that owns retries, dead-lettering, and error tracking.
- **In scope:** Booking-level ETL (one webhook = one Cal.com booking event), raw payload archival, ETL'd JSONL output to GCS, BigQuery-ready schema.
- **Out of scope (Phase 1):** Embedding/LanceDB upload, API-polling backfill, non-`BOOKING_*` webhook families (recordings, forms, meetings, OOO, etc. — all ship as Cal.com webhooks per the OpenAPI `triggers` enum, but each gets its own family in Phase 2).
- **Delivery contract:** Modal endpoints return 4xx/5xx for any failure or rejection. The middle layer surfaces these in its dashboard; no skip-as-200 semantics inside the pipeline.

## Interfaces

### Webhook endpoint

```
POST <modal-app>/export_to_gcp_etl
Content-Type: application/json
Body: BookingOutput_2024_08_13 JSON (see Cal.com OpenAPI)
```

**Decision required (default chosen):** model the request body as the `BookingOutput` directly rather than the Cal.com webhook envelope (`{triggerEvent, createdAt, payload}`). Aligns with "based on API spec." Wrap later if Cal.com signs the envelope.

Companion endpoint (Phase 1):

```
POST <modal-app>/export_to_gcp_raw         # raw dict, no validation, archival only
```

Phase 2 will add `export_to_modal_storage` and `export_to_lancedb` runners (ported from `tmp/gtm/` when embeddings are wired).

### Pydantic model surface

| Model | Cal.com schema | Required fields | Optional/notable |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Booking` | `BookingOutput_2024_08_13` | `id:int`, `uid:str`, `title:str`, `description:str`, `status:Literal["cancelled","accepted","rejected","pending"]`, `start:datetime`, `end:datetime`, `duration:int`, `eventType:EventType`, `location:str`, `absentHost:bool`, `createdAt:datetime`, `updatedAt:datetime`, `hosts:list[BookingHost]`, `attendees:list[BookingAttendee]`, `bookingFieldsResponses:dict` | `cancellationReason`, `cancelledByEmail`, `reschedulingReason`, `rescheduledByEmail`, `rescheduledFromUid`, `rescheduledToUid`, `metadata:dict\|None`, `rating`, `icsUid`, `guests:list[str]\|None`. `meetingUrl` is deprecated upstream — drop. |
| `BookingHost` | `BookingHost` | `id:int`, `name:str`, `email:str`, `displayEmail:str`, `username:str`, `timeZone:str` | — |
| `BookingAttendee` | `BookingAttendee` | `name:str`, `email:str`, `displayEmail:str`, `timeZone:str`, `absent:bool` | `language`, `phoneNumber` |
| `EventType` | `EventType` | `id:int`, `slug:str` | — |
| `RecordingItem` | `RecordingItem` | `id:str`, `roomName:str`, `startTs:int`, `status:str`, `duration:int`, `shareToken:str` | `maxParticipants`, `downloadLink` (nullable), `error` (nullable) |
| `Transcript` | helper for `GetBookingTranscriptsOutput.data` | `urls:list[str]` | — |

`Booking.get_booking_id() -> str` returns `self.uid` (Cal.com analogue of Fathom's `Recording.get_recording_id_from_url()`).

### Webhook ETL contract

Defined on `class Webhook(BaseModel)` in `src/services/caldotcom/etl/booking/webhook.py`. Static methods mirror Fathom `call/webhook.py`:

| Method | Returns |
|---|---|
| `modal_get_secret_collection_names()` | `["devx-growth-gcp"]` |
| `etl_get_bucket_name()` | `"devx-caldotcom-booking-etl"` |
| `storage_get_app_name()` | `etl_get_bucket_name()` |
| `storage_get_base_model_type()` | `None` |
| `lance_get_project_name()` | `NotImplementedError` |
| `lance_get_base_model_type()` | `NotImplementedError` |
| `etl_is_valid_webhook(self)` | `True` for `BOOKING` — declares this webhook family has a meaningful ETL representation. Returns `False` for raw-only families (none in Phase 1). NOT a per-payload status filter. |
| `etl_get_invalid_webhook_error_msg(self)` | Human-readable reason explaining "this webhook family is raw-only, ETL endpoint should not have been called" — surfaces misconfigurations in the middle layer dashboard. |
| `etl_get_json(self, storage=None)` | `flatsplode`-flattened JSONL string with `booking_uid` injected and per-row `id = f"{uid}-{n:05d}"` |
| `etl_get_file_name(self)` | `f"{clean_timestamp(start)}-{uid}-{clean_string(title)}.jsonl"` |
| `etl_get_base_models(self, storage)` | `NotImplementedError` (until lance is wired) |

## Bucket Naming Convention

All GCS buckets in `gtm-sdk` follow `devx-{platform}-{webhook_type}-{raw|etl}` (singular noun for `webhook_type`). Matches the existing `devx-octolens-mention-raw` precedent.

| Platform | Webhook type | Raw bucket | ETL bucket |
|---|---|---|---|
| `caldotcom` | `booking` | `devx-caldotcom-booking-raw` | `devx-caldotcom-booking-etl` *(Phase 1)* |
| `caldotcom` | `recording` | `devx-caldotcom-recording-raw` | `devx-caldotcom-recording-etl` *(Phase 2+)* |
| `caldotcom` | `form` | `devx-caldotcom-form-raw` | `devx-caldotcom-form-etl` *(Phase 2+)* |
| `caldotcom` | `meeting` | `devx-caldotcom-meeting-raw` | `devx-caldotcom-meeting-etl` *(Phase 2+, if not folded into `booking`)* |

Each `webhook_type` corresponds to one `etl/<webhook_type>/webhook.py` family and one runner registration. Cal.com supports configuring different webhook URLs per trigger type, so each endpoint receives exactly one payload shape — no in-process dispatcher needed.

**Raw-only families** are valid: a `webhook_type` may ship a raw bucket without an ETL bucket if its `Webhook.etl_is_valid_webhook()` returns `False`. In that case we register only the `export_to_gcp_raw` runner for that family. Cal.com `BOOKING` is **not** raw-only — it has both raw and ETL.

## Architecture

Four layers:

1. **Models** (`src/services/caldotcom/{booking,host,attendee,event_type,recording,transcript}/`) — pure Pydantic with inline `test_*` functions. No I/O, no Modal dependency.
2. **ETL** (`src/services/caldotcom/etl/<webhook_type>/webhook.py`) — `Webhook` subclass implements the contract above. Knows how to flatten itself, name itself, and report validity.
3. **Runner templates** (`src/services/runner/*.py`) — **factory functions**, not direct Modal apps. Each runner exposes `make_app(webhook_model: type[BaseModel], bucket_name: str) -> modal.App` that returns a configured Modal app. Pure templates; no hardcoded imports of `WebhookModel`.
4. **Deploy entry points** (`src/services/deploy/<platform>_<webhook_type>_<runner>.py`) — 3-line files per (family × runner) combination. Each calls the runner factory with a specific `WebhookModel` and bucket name. One Modal app per deploy file. Modal app naming uses `CloudGoogle.clean_bucket_name(bucket_name)`.

This is the **Pattern B parametrization**: the runner code is genuinely shared, but each family is deployed independently. Adding a new webhook family = one new `etl/<webhook_type>/webhook.py` model + one new `deploy/...` 3-liner per runner type. The runner files themselves do not change.

Example deploy file (`src/services/deploy/caldotcom_booking_etl.py`):

```python
from src.services.runner.export_to_gcp_etl import make_app
from src.services.caldotcom.etl.booking.webhook import Webhook

app = make_app(webhook_model=Webhook, bucket_name="devx-caldotcom-booking-etl")
```

Phase 2 family addition (e.g., `src/services/deploy/caldotcom_recording_etl.py`) is the same shape, different imports and bucket name.

## Data Flow

```
Cal.com webhook
   │ HTTP POST JSON
   ▼
Modal fastapi_endpoint (export_to_gcp_etl)
   │ Pydantic validation → Webhook instance
   ▼
Webhook.etl_is_valid_webhook()
   │ True → continue;  False → 200 with error msg, no write
   ▼
Webhook.etl_get_json()             # flatsplode flatten + inject booking_uid + row id
   │
   ▼
GCS write: gs://devx-caldotcom-booking-etl/<etl_get_file_name()>.jsonl
```

Parallel raw flow (`export_to_gcp_raw`) accepts a raw `dict`, skips validation/flattening, writes to `gs://devx-caldotcom-booking-raw/`.

## Error Handling

| Condition | Source | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Invalid JSON body | FastAPI/Pydantic | 422 with Pydantic error detail |
| Missing required field | Pydantic | 422 with field path |
| `etl_is_valid_webhook()` returns False | `Webhook.etl_is_valid_webhook` | 422 with `{status: "raw_only_family", reason: etl_get_invalid_webhook_error_msg()}` — indicates a misconfiguration where a raw-only webhook family was pointed at the ETL endpoint. Middle layer surfaces in dashboard. Cal.com `BOOKING` returns `True`, so this path is dormant in Phase 1. |
| GCP auth failure | `gcsfs` / Modal secret `devx-growth-gcp` | 500; middle layer retries per its config |
| GCS write failure (network/quota) | `gcsfs` | 500; middle layer retries |
| Duplicate webhook delivery | middle-layer redelivery | Idempotent on filename — `clean_timestamp(start)-uid` collides and overwrites |
| `lance_*` / `etl_get_base_models` invoked | `Webhook` | `NotImplementedError` — sentinel for Phase 2 wiring (no runner calls these in Phase 1) |

## File Structure

```
gtm-sdk/
  pyproject.toml                 # pytest collects test_* and integration_test_* from every .py
  requirements.txt               # modal, pydantic, polars, orjson, flatsplode, gcsfs, fastapi, uuid7
  conftest.py                    # exclude module-load secret importers
  AGENTS.md                      # adapted from tmp/gtm/AGENTS.md (fathom → caldotcom)
  src/
    services/
      caldotcom/
        __init__.py
        booking/booking.py            # Booking model + tests
        host/host.py                  # BookingHost model + tests
        attendee/attendee.py          # BookingAttendee model + tests
        event_type/event_type.py      # EventType model + tests
        recording/recording.py        # RecordingItem model + tests
        transcript/transcript.py      # Transcript wrapper + tests
        etl/
          booking/
            __init__.py
            webhook.py                # Webhook ETL contract
            bigquery_schema.json      # flattened column schema
      runner/
        export_to_gcp_etl.py          # exposes make_app(webhook_model, bucket_name) — template
        export_to_gcp_raw.py          # exposes make_app(bucket_name) — template (no model needed)
      deploy/
        caldotcom_booking_etl.py      # 3-liner: imports BookingWebhook → make_app(...)
        caldotcom_booking_raw.py      # 3-liner: bucket_name=devx-caldotcom-booking-raw
      dlt/filesystem_gcp.py           # vendored from tmp/gtm — only file the runners touch
```

**Vendor-only port (resolved 2026-04-25).** The repo ships exactly the files Cal.com Phase 1 exercises. Not ported from `tmp/gtm/src/services/`: `gemini/`, `lance/`, `local/filesystem.py`, `runner/export_to_modal_storage.py`, `runner/export_to_lancedb.py`. Phase 2 brings these in alongside their consumers.

## BigQuery schema

`src/services/caldotcom/etl/booking/bigquery_schema.json` covers the flattened columns produced by `flatsplode`:

`id`, `booking_uid`, `booking_id`, `booking_title`, `booking_description`, `booking_status`, `booking_start`, `booking_end`, `booking_duration`, `booking_location`, `event_type_id`, `event_type_slug`, `host_id`, `host_email`, `host_name`, `host_username`, `host_timezone`, `attendees_email`, `attendees_name`, `attendees_timezone`, `attendees_absent`, `attendees_phone_number`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, plus reschedule/cancel fields (`cancellation_reason`, `cancelled_by_email`, `rescheduling_reason`, `rescheduled_by_email`, `rescheduled_from_uid`, `rescheduled_to_uid`).

Final column list locked down in the plan — derived from the actual `flatsplode` output of a representative payload, not hand-curated.

## Auth & Secrets

| Secret | Source | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `devx-growth-gcp` | Modal secret collection | All runners — GCS read/write via `gcsfs` |

No Cal.com API credentials needed for Phase 1 (webhook is push-based; signature verification is a Phase 2 item once envelope wrapping is decided).

## Reuse from Existing Code

Adapted directly from `tmp/gtm/src/services/fathom/`:

| Fathom artifact | Cal.com analogue |
|---|---|
| `fathom/call/call.py` (Recording) | `caldotcom/booking/booking.py` (Booking) |
| `fathom/user/user.py` (FathomUser) | `caldotcom/host/host.py` (BookingHost) |
| `fathom/etl/call/webhook.py` | `caldotcom/etl/booking/webhook.py` |
| `Recording.get_recording_id_from_url()` | `Booking.get_booking_id()` (returns `uid`) |
| `runner/export_to_gcp_etl.py` + `export_to_gcp_raw.py` | ported with refactor: convert from hardcoded-import module to `make_app(...)` factory function. Per-family deploy files in `src/services/deploy/` consume the factory. |
| `runner/export_to_modal_storage.py` + `export_to_lancedb.py` | NOT ported in Phase 1 — vendored later when embeddings ship |
| `dlt/filesystem_gcp.py` | vendored as-is (only supporting infra Phase 1 needs) |
| `AGENTS.md` | string-replace fathom → caldotcom |

## Testing & Validation

- **Unit tests** colocated in each model file (`test_*` functions). Pytest config in `pyproject.toml` collects `test_*` and `integration_test_*` from every `.py`.
- **Fixture payloads:** capture 2-3 real Cal.com booking webhook payloads (accepted, cancelled, rescheduled) into `tests/fixtures/`. Drive `Webhook` instantiation, `etl_get_json`, and `etl_get_file_name` from these.
- **Manual validation:**
  1. Deploy `export_to_gcp_etl` Modal app.
  2. POST a fixture payload to the endpoint.
  3. Verify JSONL appears at `gs://devx-caldotcom-booking-etl/<expected-filename>.jsonl`.
  4. Run BigQuery `bq load --schema bigquery_schema.json` against the file — should succeed with zero schema errors.
- **Edge cases:** cancelled bookings (verify reschedule/cancel fields populate), bookings with empty `attendees`, bookings with `metadata: null`, duplicate webhook delivery (filename collision check).

## Success Criteria

1. POSTing a valid `BookingOutput_2024_08_13` payload to `export_to_gcp_etl` produces a JSONL file at `gs://devx-caldotcom-booking-etl/<clean_timestamp>-<uid>-<clean_title>.jsonl` within 5 seconds.
2. POSTing the same payload to `export_to_gcp_raw` produces a JSONL at `gs://devx-caldotcom-booking-raw/...` containing the unmodified payload.
3. `bq load --schema=bigquery_schema.json` against any ETL output file succeeds without schema errors.
4. All unit tests pass: `pytest src/services/caldotcom/`.
5. `etl_get_base_models` and `lance_*` raise `NotImplementedError` (Phase 1 sentinel — confirms scaffolding wired correctly).
6. Adding a new Cal.com webhook family in Phase 2 requires: one `etl/<webhook_type>/webhook.py` model file, one 3-line `deploy/caldotcom_<webhook_type>_etl.py` (and matching `_raw.py`), two new GCS buckets (`gcloud storage buckets create`), and a Cal.com webhook subscription. **The runner template files themselves are not modified.**

## Future Considerations (Phase 2+)

- **Embeddings:** wire `lance_get_project_name` / `lance_get_base_model_type` and implement `etl_get_base_models` for Cal.com booking text fields.
- **API polling backfill:** Cal.com analogue of Fathom's `backfill.py` to pull historical bookings via REST.
- **Additional webhook types as new families:** each new Cal.com trigger type is a new `etl/<webhook_type>/` family with its own bucket pair (`devx-caldotcom-<webhook_type>-{raw,etl}`) and runner registration. Same architecture as `etl/booking/`, no dispatcher. Phase 2 candidates: `etl/recording/` (`RECORDING_READY`, `RECORDING_TRANSCRIPTION_GENERATED`), `etl/form/` (`FORM_SUBMITTED`), `etl/meeting/` (`MEETING_STARTED`/`MEETING_ENDED` if their fields don't fit `BookingOutput`).
- **Webhook envelope wrapping:** if Cal.com adds signed `{triggerEvent, createdAt, payload}` envelopes, switch the request body model and verify signatures.
- **Validity rules:** revisit `etl_is_valid_webhook` to optionally reject `status="cancelled"` once downstream consumers signal preference.

## Open Questions

1. ~~**Webhook payload shape:** model `BookingOutput` directly *(default)* or wrap in `{triggerEvent, createdAt, payload}`?~~ **Resolved (2026-04-25):** model `BookingOutput` directly. Signature verification deferred to Phase 2 if Cal.com adds signed envelopes.
2. ~~**Supporting infra port:** wholesale from `tmp/gtm/src/services/{dlt,local,gemini,lance,runner}/` *(default)* or vendor only the runner files Cal.com touches?~~ **Resolved (2026-04-25):** vendor-only. Ship `runner/export_to_gcp_etl.py`, `runner/export_to_gcp_raw.py`, and `dlt/filesystem_gcp.py`. Phase 2 brings the rest.
3. ~~**Bucket names final:** `devx-caldotcom-booking-etl` / `devx-caldotcom-booking-raw`?~~ **Resolved (2026-04-25):** yes, singular `booking`, matching `devx-{platform}-{webhook_type}-{raw|etl}` convention (precedent: `devx-octolens-mention-raw`). Phase 2 trigger families get sibling bucket pairs.
4. ~~**Validity rule:** accept all statuses *(default)* or reject `status="cancelled"`?~~ **Resolved (2026-04-25):** the original framing was wrong. `etl_is_valid_webhook` is **not** a per-payload status filter — it's a class-level ETL eligibility gate ("does this webhook family have a meaningful ETL representation, or is it raw-only?"). For Cal.com `BOOKING`: returns `True`. Status-based filtering, if ever needed, happens downstream in BigQuery.
5. ~~**Recordings/transcripts submodule:** confirm deferred to Phase 2.~~ **Resolved (2026-04-25):** deferred. Phase 1 ships only `caldotcom_booking_{etl,raw}` deploys. The factory + deploy-file pattern means Phase 2 family addition is a 3-liner per runner — no runner template changes — so the deferral has near-zero architectural cost.

## Resolved Design Decisions

Captured here so the rationale survives even after the open question is struck through.

| Decision | Choice | Date |
|---|---|---|
| Webhook payload shape | Model `BookingOutput` directly (no envelope wrapping) | 2026-04-25 |
| One-line `WebhookModel` swap | Yes — locked as success criterion #6 | 2026-04-25 |
| Failure semantics | Modal returns 4xx/5xx; webhook middle layer (Hookdeck-style) owns retries, dead-lettering, and error tracking. No skip-as-200. | 2026-04-25 |
| Supporting infra port | Vendor-only. Phase 1 ports `runner/export_to_gcp_etl.py`, `runner/export_to_gcp_raw.py`, `dlt/filesystem_gcp.py`. `gemini/`, `lance/`, `local/`, and the other two runners stay in `tmp/gtm/` until Phase 2. | 2026-04-25 |
| Bucket naming convention | `devx-{platform}-{webhook_type}-{raw\|etl}`, singular `webhook_type`. Phase 1: `devx-caldotcom-booking-{raw,etl}`. Each new Cal.com trigger family adds a sibling bucket pair, not a dispatcher. | 2026-04-25 |
| Purpose of `etl_is_valid_webhook` | Class-level ETL eligibility gate for the webhook family — `True` means "ship raw + ETL," `False` means "raw-only family, no ETL bucket." NOT a per-payload status filter. Cal.com `BOOKING` returns `True`. Downstream filtering (e.g., excluding cancelled bookings) is a BigQuery-layer concern, not a pipeline-layer concern. | 2026-04-25 |
| Runner parametrization (Pattern B) | Runner files are factory functions `make_app(webhook_model, bucket_name) -> modal.App`. Per-family deploy files in `src/services/deploy/` consume the factory. Each family = N Modal apps (one per runner type), but runner code is shared. Refactor-on-port the Fathom runners to this shape. | 2026-04-25 |
| Phase 1 scope = booking only | Ship `caldotcom_booking_etl` and `caldotcom_booking_raw` deploys only. All other webhook families (recording, form, meeting, OOO, etc.) are Phase 2 — each is a model file + 3-line deploy file + bucket pair. | 2026-04-25 |
